es: Formular preguntas de coaching abiertas e hipotéticas (What would it take to...?, What's stopping you from...?) en lugar de dar consejos directos.

teaching.en: A coach rarely gives advice; instead she asks, What would it take to reach a goal that you set for this month?
teaching.es: Un coach rara vez da consejos; en cambio pregunta: ¿qué haría falta para alcanzar una meta que te fijaste para este mes?
teaching.explanationEs: What would it take to + verbo: pregunta abierta sobre lo necesario.
segments: A coach rarely gives advice; instead she asks, What would it
take to reach a goal that you set for this month?
teaching.audioText: A coach rarely gives advice; instead she asks, What would it take to reach a goal that you set for this month?

teaching.en: What is the biggest obstacle for you right now, and which option feels more realistic given your week?
teaching.es: ¿Cuál es el mayor obstáculo para ti ahora mismo, y qué opción te parece más realista dada tu semana?
teaching.explanationEs: Pregunta abierta con What y Which: no se contesta con sí o no.
segments: What is the biggest obstacle for you right now,
and which option feels more realistic given your week?
teaching.audioText: What is the biggest obstacle for you right now, and which option feels more realistic given your week?

teaching.en: How would you feel if you could make progress this week, and what would make you more confident?
teaching.es: ¿Cómo te sentirías si pudieras avanzar esta semana, y qué te haría sentirte más seguro?
teaching.explanationEs: Pregunta hipotética: would + if + pasado simple (could).
segments: How would you feel if you could make progress
this week, and what would make you more confident?
teaching.audioText: How would you feel if you could make progress this week, and what would make you more confident?

teaching.en: What would you do if you were more confident, and what small first step could you take tomorrow morning?
teaching.es: ¿Qué harías si fueras más seguro de ti mismo, y qué pequeño primer paso podrías dar mañana por la mañana?
teaching.explanationEs: If + pasado simple (were) imagina un escenario; take a step = dar un paso.
segments: What would you do if you were more confident, and
what small first step could you take tomorrow morning?
teaching.audioText: What would you do if you were more confident, and what small first step could you take tomorrow morning?

teaching.en: What's stopping you from speaking in front of the group, and what might hold back your best ideas?
teaching.es: ¿Qué te impide hablar delante del grupo, y qué podría frenar tus mejores ideas?
teaching.explanationEs: What's stopping you from + -ing: busca el obstáculo real.
segments: What's stopping you from speaking in front of the
group, and what might hold back your best ideas?
teaching.audioText: What's stopping you from speaking in front of the group, and what might hold back your best ideas?

teaching.en: A good question can reveal a blind spot or push you out of your comfort zone, so ask it as a real option, not a hidden order.
teaching.es: Una buena pregunta puede revelar un punto ciego o sacarte de tu zona de confort, así que formúlala como una opción real, no como una orden encubierta.
teaching.explanationEs: Evita Why don't you...?: suena a pregunta, pero es un consejo disfrazado.
segments: A good question can reveal a blind spot or push you out of your
comfort zone, so ask it as a real option, not a hidden order.
teaching.audioText: A good question can reveal a blind spot or push you out of your comfort zone, so ask it as a real option, not a hidden order.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál de estas es una pregunta de coaching abierta, no un consejo ni un sí o no?

choices.text: Do you think you can reach your goal this month?
What would it take to reach a goal this month?
Why don't you just set a smaller goal this month?

feedback.es: Solo «What would it take…?» es abierta: no se responde con sí o no ni esconde un consejo.

hint.es: Descarta la que se responde con sí o no y la que suena a consejo.

prompt.es: Completa: «¿Qué te impide hablar delante del grupo?»

feedback.es: What's stopping you from + -ing busca el obstáculo real que frena a la persona.

hint.es: Es el verbo en -ing que va antes de you from.

origin.text: The player says that she wants to be more confident. Her coach answers with a question instead of advice: What's ___ you from speaking in front of the group?

prompt.es: Ordena: «¿Qué harías si fueras más seguro de ti mismo?»

answer.text: What would you do if you were more confident

feedback.es: La pregunta hipotética une would en la principal con el pasado simple (were) tras if.

hint.es: Empieza con What would you do y usa were tras if.

prompt.es: Escucha la sesión y elige qué hace la entrenadora en lugar de dar un consejo.

choices.text: She explains why mistakes are part of the game.
She warns him that the school team will not wait.
She asks questions that help him name his own problem.

feedback.es: La entrenadora pregunta en vez de aconsejar, y así él mismo nombra su problema (el miedo a equivocarse).

origin.audio: A volunteer coach was talking to a boy who wanted to join the school team but kept finding excuses. She did not tell him to try harder. Instead, she asked: What's stopping you from going to the first training? He said he was afraid of making mistakes in front of the others. So she asked another question: What would it take for you to feel more confident? After a pause he answered that he could ask a friend to come with him. The coach simply smiled.

prompt.es: Con la misma sesión, elige qué sugiere la sonrisa final de la entrenadora.

choices.text: That the idea came from him, which is exactly what she hoped for.
That she thinks his plan is too simple for him.
That she had already decided to invite his friend.

feedback.es: Sonríe porque la solución (llevar a un amigo) la encontró él: es lo que busca una pregunta de coaching.

origin.audio: A volunteer coach was talking to a boy who wanted to join the school team but kept finding excuses. She did not tell him to try harder. Instead, she asked: What's stopping you from going to the first training? He said he was afraid of making mistakes in front of the others. So she asked another question: What would it take for you to feel more confident? After a pause he answered that he could ask a friend to come with him. The coach simply smiled.

prompt.es: Completa: «Es más fácil hallar una solución cuando puedes nombrar el mayor obstáculo.»

feedback.es: Obstacle es lo que se interpone en el camino; nombrarlo es el primer paso de una buena pregunta de coaching.

origin.text: Most people already know part of the answer. It is easier to find a solution once you can name the biggest ___ in your way.

prompt.es: Escribe dos preguntas de coaching para que el jugador supere su miedo.

answer.text: What's stopping you from speaking in front of the group? What would it take for you to feel more confident?
accepted: What's stopping you from speaking in front of the group? What would it take for you to feel more confident?
What is stopping you from speaking in front of the group? What would it take to be more confident?
What's stopping you from speaking in front of the others? What would it take for you to be more confident?

feedback.es: Dos preguntas abiertas, una sobre el obstáculo (What's stopping you from...?) y otra hipotética (What would it take...?), sin dar consejos.

origin.text: Un jugador te dice: «Quiero hablar delante del grupo, pero me paralizo.» No le des consejos. Escribe dos preguntas abiertas: una con What's stopping you from... y otra con What would it take...

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué funcionó mejor el segundo entrenador.

choices.text: The second coach gave more detailed advice than the first.
The player found her own solution instead of receiving orders.
The player felt more pressure to practise every day.

feedback.es: La jugadora encuentra su propia solución (usar el descanso); al primero solo le dieron órdenes y no hizo nada.

origin.audio: Two coaches talked to the same player. The first said: You should practise every day, and you should stop worrying. The player nodded but did nothing. The second asked: What would help you to practise three times this week? The player thought for a moment, then said she could use her lunch break. She wrote it down and looked surprised at how simple it was.

prompt.es: Con la misma escena, elige qué sugiere que la jugadora «looked surprised».

choices.text: That she disagreed with the question that the coach had asked.
That she was shocked by how much practice was needed.
That she had not expected to find an answer so easily.

feedback.es: La sorpresa se refiere a lo simple que era la solución, no al desacuerdo ni al esfuerzo requerido.

origin.audio: Two coaches talked to the same player. The first said: You should practise every day, and you should stop worrying. The player nodded but did nothing. The second asked: What would help you to practise three times this week? The player thought for a moment, then said she could use her lunch break. She wrote it down and looked surprised at how simple it was.

prompt.es: Completa: «¿Qué haría falta para hablar con ella?»

feedback.es: What would it take to + verbo es la pregunta abierta que sustituye al consejo disfrazado.

origin.text: Why don't you talk to her? sounds like a question, but it is really advice in disguise. A better version is: What would it ___ to talk to her?

prompt.es: Lee lo que dice el adolescente y elige la respuesta que es una pregunta de coaching.

choices.text: What's stopping you from finishing one small thing this week?
You should finish one small thing every week, starting today.
Why don't you ask a friend to check your work every day?

feedback.es: Solo «What's stopping you…?» es una pregunta abierta; las otras son consejos, aunque una suene a pregunta.

origin.text: A boy tells his coach: I never finish anything, and I do not know why.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige con qué fin hace la entrenadora la segunda pregunta.

choices.text: To tell the youngest player that feeling nervous is a weakness.
To help the players turn their worry into something useful.
To move the conversation away from winning the match.

feedback.es: La segunda pregunta parte de la emoción de la jugadora y busca convertirla en algo útil, sin juzgarla.

origin.audio: At the end of the session, the coach asked the team: How would you feel if we won the next match? Nobody answered at first. Then the youngest player said that she would feel proud, but also nervous. The coach wrote both words on the board and asked: What would help us turn the nervous feeling into energy?

prompt.es: Completa: «¿Qué opción es más realista esta semana: una sesión larga o tres cortas?»

feedback.es: Realistic describe lo que se puede cumplir en la práctica; una buena pregunta ayuda a elegir una opción realista.

origin.text: You cannot do everything at once. Which option feels more ___ for you this week: one long session or three short ones?
